A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gaussian Eigen Models for Human Heads. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V2 reports original novel-view, expression, reenactment, and compression experiments, including NeRSemble results and the Multiface evaluation in Appendix E.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds test-sequence refinement results and a qualitative glasses example.

M1.justification: The PCA distillation, QR-based refinement, losses, and image-based regressor remain unchanged. V3's optional feature-texture note in Appendix B adds implementation documentation without establishing a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain NeRSemble and Multiface coverage. V3 adds a qualitative reconstruction example involving an avatar wearing glasses, extending accessory/topology coverage in Section 4.3 and Figure 9.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain Gaussian Avatars, Animatable Gaussians, and INSTA. The appendix also retains PointAvatar and AvatarMAV, matching v2 Figure 14 to v3 Figure 15. The newly discussed Gaussian blendshapes work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 adds a controlled comparison with and without refinement on two randomly selected test sequences. Existing benchmark splits, image resolution, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged; the addition does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 reports refinement benefits on training images; v3 additionally tests whether refinement helps on test sequences. V3 also adds the glasses topology case study. Existing compression and regressor-input ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Selecting two test sequences for the new refinement comparison changes the evaluation sample, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V3 newly reports PSNR/LPIPS/SSIM of 31.51/0.091/0.936 with refinement versus 31.38/0.094/0.933 without refinement. It adds glasses renderings and omits one qualitative example row from each of Figures 5 and 6. All seven tables and the appendix heatmap values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, PCA definitions, coefficient constraints, deformation-gradient reasoning, and Gaussian-splatting preliminaries are unchanged. The added explanation of fixed colors introduces no new formal assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: lightweight Gaussian eigenbasis distillation and real-time image-driven animation. The expanded conclusion reiterates RGB control and adjustable memory–quality trade-offs already described in v2.

C2.justification: V3 explains how fixed colors preserve Gaussian semantic correspondence for PCA, interprets the added refinement check as showing no overfitting, and identifies unstable expressions under side-view generalization as a limitation. The earlier global-basis and personalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 newly states that eigenbasis construction takes approximately one minute and documents optional feature-texture concatenation with rasterized normals in Appendix B. Existing optimizer, training budget, hardware information, and promised code/model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Ma et al.'s 3D Gaussian Blendshapes and distinguishes its 3DMM-dependent control from GEM. Section 5 also identifies the previously cited Synthetic Prior for Few-Shot Drivable Head Avatar Inversion as a potential compression target.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized additions and edits to the method explanation, evaluation discussion, limitations, conclusion, and acknowledgements. Most prose, the main section sequence, and the appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figure 9 for glasses, reduces Figures 5 and 6 from four displayed example rows to three, and rearranges several tables and surrounding text. The earlier Figure 9 and appendix figures are retained with subsequent numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 supports refinement primarily with training scores; v3 adds a small test-sequence check, improving evidence about generalization. Clearer fixed-color reasoning and an explicit side-view failure limitation also improve understanding. These limited gains outweigh the omission of two qualitative example rows, while the main quantitative evidence and appendix evaluations remain intact.
